posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
[http://www.cobolt.se/index.asp](http://www.cobolt.se/index.asp) 

This company has single longitudinal mode 473nm DPSS lasers up to 50mW. Not certain if they're good for holography, but has anyone heard about prices?

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Don't know about prices, but would make a wild guess that they would be in the 4-6K$ range if they are to be at all competitive with similar products available from Roithner. [http://www.roithner-laser.com/](http://www.roithner-laser.com/)

I found this description of their multiline DPSS (simultaneous 491 and 532 nm using periodically poled KTP) interesting.

[http://www.cobolt.se/news.asp](http://www.cobolt.se/news.asp)

posts.author: edelbrp
posts.content_md:
The dual-Calypso looks interesting, too. Although I doubt it has much of a cohoerence length (or else they might have mentioned it!).

BTW- I searched Google and couldn't find any pricing on their products. But, at least it's good to see yet-another producer of hologram capable lasers to compete and drive the price down.

BBTW- Speaking of Google, Keyhole has turned into [http://earth.google.com](http://earth.google.com) and is now free. If you have a PeeCee running WindowsXP, you can play with some pretty incredible satellite picture zooming software. I think I saw my car parked in the lot at my work. Cooool! ;')
